_comment: EXTERNAL CLAIMS LEDGER (front-website Gate 3b, audit B). Every assertion this site makes ABOUT A THIRD PARTY lives here, with the source that supports it and the date it was checked. Rendered only through App\Support\Marketing\MarketingClaims; guarded by MarketingClaimsTest + CI Gate 6. A claim with source_url null is UNSOURCED and may not publish. A claim past review_by is STALE and reds the build — because a competitor changes their pricing without telling us, and nothing else in this system would ever notice.
_status: AWAITING SOURCES — the founder supplies source_url + verified_on + review_by per claim. Until then every entry is unpublishable and the two pages carrying them stay held.

_schema.subject: the third party the claim is about
_schema.claim: the exact assertion, as it would appear
_schema.source_url: a public page that supports it — null until supplied
_schema.verified_on: YYYY-MM-DD the source was actually read — null until supplied
_schema.review_by: YYYY-MM-DD after which the claim must be re-checked — null until supplied
_schema.disposition: publish | soften | remove — what audit B ruled for this claim

claims.subject: Mews
claims.claim: API-first architecture and a large integration marketplace; built for boutique hotels and groups with technical resourcing.
claims.note: The API and marketplace are publicly documented. 'Large' is a judgement — soften to a factual count, or quote the vendor's own wording.

claims.subject: Cloudbeds
claims.claim: PMS, channel manager, booking engine and payments bundled under one subscription, with a broad installed base among independent properties.
claims.note: The bundle is on their public site. 'Broad installed base' is an unsourced MARKET claim — cite a published figure or drop that clause.

claims.subject: Guesty
claims.claim: Vacation-rental automation and marketplace distribution depth; built for short-term rental managers at scale.
claims.note: Cite the vendor's own positioning page; the wording is close to how they describe themselves.

claims.subject: Hostaway
claims.claim: Automation without heavy setup; built for growing rental portfolios.
claims.note: 'Without heavy setup' is a claim about ANOTHER PRODUCT'S EASE OF USE. No public page establishes it and we have not run their onboarding — it cannot be sourced, only tested. Soften to their own positioning, or drop the setup clause.

claims.subject: the PMS market
claims.claim: Per unit, the market clusters in a similar band and we sit inside it.
claims.note: An unsourced claim about COMPETITOR PRICING — the sharpest legal exposure and the fastest decay on the page. Recommend REMOVAL: nothing is gained that a statement about our own pricing does not say, without asserting anything about anyone else. NOTE ALSO: it says 'per unit', which is no longer even true of us — billing charges flat (B12).

claims.subject: Mews, Cloudbeds, Guesty, Hostaway
claims.claim: Some platforms bundle a booking engine; others expect you to bring one from their marketplace.
claims.note: Checkable per vendor from public product pages. Needs one source PER vendor, not one for the sentence.

claims.subject: the page's own disclaimer
claims.claim: Positioning on this page reflects publicly available category analysis at the time of writing.
claims.note: UNFALSIFIABLE AS DRAWN. 'At the time of writing' with no date can never be shown stale, so it ages invisibly forever. A real date is mandatory — this ledger's verified_on becomes it.

claims.subject: OTAs (Booking.com, Airbnb, Expedia)
claims.note: The single most load-bearing number on the page. Sourceable — the marketplaces publish commission structures — but rates vary by market, property type and programme (a Preferred Partner pays more), so the citation must state the basis and review_by should be short.

claims.subject: OTAs / channel-manager stacks (categories, unnamed)
claims.claim: Side-by-side table: OTAs lack a booking engine, front desk, housekeeping board and owner statements; a channel-manager stack has them as add-ons, separate apps or manual work.
claims.note: A CATEGORY generalisation naming no specific product — the lowest-risk item here. Keep it categorical; the moment a vendor is named in a cell it becomes a per-vendor claim needing a per-vendor source.

claims.subject: Airbnb
claims.claim: If you run one apartment and Airbnb sends you all the bookings you want, a PMS is overhead. Stay where you are.
claims.note: Advice AGAINST buying, asserting nothing about Airbnb's product. Arguably needs no source at all; ledgered so the sweep stays complete.

claims.subject: the page itself
claims.claim: (absent) — Compare names five companies and carries NO disclaimer, NO trademark notice and NO date.
claims.note: NOT A CLAIM TO SOURCE — a MISSING SAFEGUARD to add. Compare needs the same disclaimer + trademark notice Alternatives already carries, dated.

claims.subject: the page's own disclaimer
claims.claim: We have not tested these products against ours, and none of the vendors named have reviewed this page.
claims.note: THIS ONE STAYS AND NEEDS NO EXTERNAL SOURCE — it is TRUE, it is about us, and sourcing the other claims from public pages does not make it false. Ledgered so nobody 'tidies' it away when the sources land.
